disclaimer: These status corrections report results attributed to existing papers or to the final source version. Graph-Theory-LLM-Proofs located and checked the implication; it is not credited as the author of the result.

results.name: AX_plane_triangle_free_distant_precoloring_extension
results.one_line: The final source version records that Dvořák and Lidický proved Conjecture 1.5, while its Theorem 5.1 proves that Conjecture 1.5 implies Conjecture 1.4.
results.caveats: This is a literature-status correction rather than an independent proof; the supplied material does not reproduce the proof or an explicit value of d.
results.article_title: Three-coloring triangle-free graphs on surfaces V. Coloring planar graphs with distant anomalies

results.name: AX_girth_5_planar_list_critical_bounded
results.one_line: Postle's fixed-surface bound for fixed-list critical girth-five graphs implies the conjecture after singleton lists are replaced by constant-genus three-list forcing gadgets.
results.caveats: The required input is the uniform fixed-list L-critical theorem, not merely finiteness of underlying choice-critical graphs.
results.article_title: 3 List Coloring Graphs of Girth at least Five on Surfaces

results.name: AX_identifying_codes_hereditary_vc_dimension_dichotomy
results.one_line: The intended finite-VC-dimension implication is already refuted by the hereditary class of C4-free bipartite graphs in Theorem 4.3 of the cited source.
results.caveats: The inapproximability is conditional on the theorem's standard complexity assumption, and the extracted phrase 'logarithmic lower bound' is formally imprecise.
results.article_title: Identifying codes in hereditary classes of graphs and VC-dimension

results.name: AX_z5_antisymmetric_flow_edge_connected_digraphs
results.one_line: Corollary 13(iv) of the source paper proves that every directed 12-edge-connected graph has a $\mathbb{Z}_5$-antisymmetric flow, directly establishing the requested constant.
results.article_title: Additive bases and flows in graphs
results.article_authors: Louis Esperet, Rémi de Joannis de Verclos, Tien-Nam Le, Stéphan Thomassé

results.name: AX_capture_time_higher_genus_bounds
results.one_line: Yes: the finite-state bound gives capt_k(G) <= n^{c(G)+1} for every k >= c(G), and hence Schroeder's conjecture immediately yields capt_k(G) <= n^{g+4}.
results.caveats: This does not prove Schroeder's conjecture or any sharper surface-specific capture-time bound.
results.article_title: Topological directions in Cops and Robbers

results.name: AX_erdos_posa_treewidth_packing_k_log_k
results.one_line: A 2019 theorem of Cames van Batenburg, Huynh, Joret, and Raymond gives an O_H(k log(k+1)) vertex Erdős–Pósa bound for every fixed planar H, and taking H to be a grid proves the conjecture.
results.caveats: The deduction is complete but relies on the published planar-minor Erdős–Pósa theorem rather than reproving it; the catalog appears to have missed arXiv:1807.04969.
results.article_title: A tight Erdős–Pósa function for planar minors

results.name: AX_dense_bipartite_induced_or_large_clique
results.one_line: The quoted fixed-clique-number theorem implies the conjecture by a staircase diagonalization, even with x_2(d)=x_3(d).
results.caveats: This relies on the prompt's claim that the Kwan-Sudakov-Tran theorem holds for every fixed t; a triangle-free-only result would not suffice.
results.article_title: Dense induced bipartite subgraphs in triangle-free graphs

results.name: AX_dense_bipartite_induced_large_girth
results.one_line: The quoted Kwan–Sudakov–Tran theorem with t=3 immediately implies the conjecture, because girth at least 4 implies triangle-freeness and their lower bound eventually exceeds 3.
results.caveats: This uses the Kwan–Sudakov–Tran theorem exactly as quoted; even if their conclusion is stated in terms of average degree, a standard pruning argument still suffices.
results.article_title: Dense induced bipartite subgraphs in triangle-free graphs

results.name: AX_planar_c4_c5_fractional_chromatic_11_3
results.one_line: The Xu–Zhu theorem quoted in the catalog gives the strictly better universal bound χ_f(G)≤7/2=11/3−1/6, thereby confirming the informal conjecture.
results.caveats: The deduction is complete, but it relies on the stated 2025 DP-coloring theorem, whose preprint and proof I have not independently inspected here; the exact optimal constant remains open.
results.article_title: Planar graphs without cycles of length 4 or 5 are (7m:2m)-DP-colorable

results.name: AX_short_rainbow_circuits_matroids
results.one_line: As written, the conjecture is false: the uniformly colored matroid U_{n-1,2n} has no circuit shorter than n.
results.caveats: This does not address variants restricted to binary or regular matroids, since the uniform counterexamples used here are not binary.
results.article_title: Short rainbow cycles in graphs and matroids

results.name: AX_online_ramsey_off_diagonal_alteration_bound
results.one_line: For every fixed m≥3, Guo and Warnke proved the natural exponent-level extension r̃(m,n)≥n^{m-o(1)}, although the original remark specified no logarithmic factor.
results.caveats: Resolution is for fixed m and the standard exponent-level interpretation; the literal informal sentence has no unique quantitative meaning.
results.article_title: Bounds on Ramsey Games via Alterations

results.name: AX_gnp_subgraph_count_anticoncentration_bound
results.one_line: The universal conjecture is false: for H = 2K2 there are x_n with Pr(X_H = x_n) = Omega(n^{-5/2}), whereas Var(X_H) = Theta(n^6), so the conjecture would require O(n^{-3}).
results.caveats: The counterexample below is self-contained for ordinary non-induced subgraph counts; the positive connected case is cited rather than reproved.
results.article_title: Combinatorial anti-concentration inequalities, with applications

results.name: AX_prism_pyramid_theta_wheel_free_separators
results.one_line: Every turtle contains an induced even wheel, so the cited n^18 bound for (theta, pyramid, prism, turtle)-free graphs applies directly.
results.caveats: This uses the standard adjacent-centers definition of a turtle from arXiv:2005.05042 and the theorem quoted in the prompt.
results.article_title: Graphs with polynomially many minimal separators

results.name: AX_even_hole_k4_diamond_free_treewidth
results.one_line: Yes: a later theorem states that every even-hole-free graph of sufficiently large treewidth contains an induced diamond or a K4.
results.caveats: The deep later structure theorem is used as a black box, and no explicit numerical treewidth bound is extracted.
results.article_title: Induced subgraphs and tree decompositions XI. Local structure in even-hole-free graphs of large treewidth

results.name: AX_planar_recoloring_girth_5_six_colors
results.one_line: The published follow-up arXiv:2112.00631 proves that the 6-recolouring graph of every n-vertex planar graph of girth at least five has diameter O(n), exactly resolving Conjecture 5.
results.caveats: This is a literature resolution; the follow-up's discharging proof is not reproduced or independently audited here.
results.article_title: Recolouring planar graphs of girth at least five

results.name: AX_intersection_graphs_polynomial_weak_coloring_numbers
results.one_line: The source paper itself proves polynomial bounds for the homothet and ball-like cases and gives an exponential counterexample for comparable boxes in dimension three.
results.caveats: The conclusion fixes the geometric parameters as in the source; any restriction excluding the three-dimensional comparable-box construction is a different question.
results.article_title: Weak Coloring Numbers of Intersection Graphs

results.name: AX_rodl_h_free_restricted_union_cover
results.one_line: The partition theorem stated in the source paper immediately gives the requested union cover, because every partition is a cover.
results.caveats: This assumes the catalog uses the same induced-H-free and ε-restricted definitions and the same dependence N=N(H,ε) as the quoted source.
results.article_title: Strengthening Rödl's theorem

results.name: AX_odd_dicycle_free_digraph_dichromatic_bounded
results.one_line: The answer is negative: the t=4 case of the cited fixed-length-cycle theorem gives bounded-clique digraphs with unbounded dichromatic number and no odd induced directed cycle.
results.caveats: This is a direct corollary of the theorem reported for arXiv:2203.15575, not a new proof of its construction.
results.article_title: Digraphs with all induced directed cycles of the same length are not dichromatically bounded

results.name: AX_lazy_transpositions_shuffle_t_counters_exact
results.one_line: The proposed identity is false: the source paper's bound for full shuffles already gives strict counterexamples, and these also yield counterexamples with t=n-1<n.
results.caveats: This settles the yes/no question, not the exact values of U_t(n) for t>=3.
results.article_title: Perfect shuffling with fewer lazy transpositions

results.name: AX_reachability_network_2_uniformity_lazy_transpositions
results.one_line: The conjecture is true: a support-plus-rank potential gives the lower bound 2n-3, matching the stated construction, and the current source note already reports a resolution.
results.caveats: The proof below is self-contained; I have not independently verified the bibliographic attribution of the post-v1 proof.
results.article_title: Short reachability networks

results.name: AX_clean_classes_finite_family_characterization
results.one_line: The literal question is answered by the published array criterion: the H-free class is clean exactly when H-free n-arrays exist for only finitely many n.
results.caveats: This is not a direct finite structural classification of the forbidden family, and no new proof of the deep array theorem is given here.
results.article_title: Induced subgraphs and tree decompositions XIII. Basic obstructions in H-free graphs for finite H

results.name: AX_prime_cayley_graph_joined_union_decomposition
results.one_line: For finite simple graphs, a nontrivial joined-union decomposition exists exactly when the graph has a proper nonsingleton module; this is polynomial-time decidable, while P4 shows that not every graph decomposes.
results.caveats: This uses the standard graph-substitution meaning of joined union; infinite graphs and more restrictive decomposition notions are not addressed.
results.article_title: On prime Cayley graphs

results.name: AX_prime_cayley_graph_finite_ring_characterization
results.one_line: For |R|≥3, Theorem 4.35 already characterizes X_R as prime exactly when R is semisimple, is not a field, and has at most one Wedderburn factor isomorphic to F₂.
results.caveats: This uses the standard unitary Cayley graph of a finite unital ring; R = F₂ gives K₂, whose status depends on the small-graph convention.
results.article_title: On prime Cayley graphs

results.name: AX_prime_cayley_graph_tensor_product_complete
results.one_line: With prime meaning module-prime, and apart from convention-dependent graphs of order at most two, the product is prime exactly when d is at least two, every n_i is at least two, and at most one n_i equals two.
results.caveats: The only ambiguity concerns whether graphs on one or two vertices are called prime.
results.article_title: On prime Cayley graphs

results.name: AX_weightable_digraphs_np_characterization
results.one_line: Assuming the catalog's stated 2026 result is accurate, polynomial-time recognition puts weightability in P and hence in NP, while independently weightability is equivalent to admitting a 0–1 edge set meeting every directed cycle exactly once.
results.caveats: The cited 2026 preprint and its bit-model algorithm were not independently checked, and its construction operations are not reproduced here.
results.article_title: When all directed cycles have the same weight

results.name: AX_large_treewidth_unavoidable_induced_subgraphs
results.one_line: A theorem of Alecu, Bonnet, Bureo Villafana, and Trotignon implies that every proper hereditary candidate obstruction family fails, so the only universal hereditary core is the tautological class of all graphs.
results.caveats: Question 1.1 is open-ended; the negative resolution concerns the universal hereditary-core formulation, while restricted-class structure theory remains open.
results.article_title: Every Graph is Essential to Large Treewidth

results.name: AX_c4_orientations_eulerian_avoidable
results.one_line: Lei, Wang, Xu, and Yang classify the Eulerian-avoidability of all orientations of $C_4$ and prove that the one-directed $K_{2,2}$ is not Eulerian-avoidable; hence not every orientation of $C_4$ is Eulerian-avoidable.
results.article_title: Avoidability of Digraphs with Height Functions and Orientations of $C_4$
results.article_authors: Hui Lei, Xiaoyi Wang, Zhijun Xu, Zhenyu Yang

results.name: AX_arithmetic_progression_packing_primes_asymptotic
results.one_line: Hou, Liu, and Zhao prove $M_{\mathbb{P}(n)}(n)=(\frac16+o(1))n^3/\ln n$, settling Conjecture 4 with its predicted constant.
results.article_title: Asymptotically optimal packings of arithmetic progressions with prime differences
results.article_authors: Jianfeng Hou, Siyue Liu, Hongbin Zhao

results.name: AX_arithmetic_progression_packing_fixed_n
results.one_line: Mao, Wang, Wei, and Yang prove $M_k(n)=(1+o(1))nk$ for every fixed $n$, confirming Conjecture 7.
results.article_title: Solution to a conjecture of Alon, Dębski, Grytczuk and Przybyło on fixed-cardinality arithmetic progressions
results.article_authors: Yaping Mao, Zhao Wang, Meiqin Wei, Gang Yang

results.name: OPG_k_edge_outerplanar_embedding_polynomial
results.one_line: Yu proves that the minimum edge-outerplanarity of a planar graph can be computed in polynomial time, answering Bentz's question affirmatively.
results.article_title: Minimum Edge-Outerplanar Embeddings are Polynomial-Time Computable

results.name: OPG_edge_imbalance_multiset_graphic
results.one_line: Schreib and Yavari prove that the positive imbalance multiset $M_G$ is graphic, establishing the imbalance conjecture in full.
results.article_title: A Proof of the Imbalance Conjecture

results.name: OPG_0_2_graphs_chromatic_number_3
results.one_line: Williamson proves that every finite three-colourable $(0,2)$-graph is bipartite; consequently no finite $(0,2)$-graph has chromatic number exactly three.
results.article_title: Finite Three-Colourable (0,2)-Graphs Are Bipartite

ai_results.name: AX_fair_representation_bipartite_matching_under_representation
ai_results.one_line: The conjecture holds with the explicit crude bound c(m)=32(m+1)^3, by combining Carathéodory reduction with proportional-necklace interpolation between two matchings.

ai_results.name: AX_large_chromatic_induced_path_uniquely_covered
ai_results.one_line: For every s at least 3, there are triangle-free graphs of arbitrarily large chromatic number with a stable-set cover for which no s-vertex induced path has the required private-cover property.

ai_results.name: AX_fractional_dichromatic_number_complexity
ai_results.one_line: For digraphs allowing digons, the p=2 problem is NP-complete via a two-layer construction in which matching digons force every weight-2 fractional colouring to encode an ordinary acyclic 2-colouring.

ai_results.name: AX_directed_kneser_graphs_existence
ai_results.one_line: For positive integers, such a digraph exists exactly when b is at most 2 or k is at most b+1; in particular, (k,b)=(5,3) is impossible.

ai_results.name: AX_lipschitz_bijection_dictator_xor_inverse
ai_results.one_line: No: every such bijection satisfies n <= 1+(k-1)+...+(k-1)^(D-1), where D is its inverse Lipschitz constant, and linear 2-Lipschitz tree maps attain the resulting bound.

ai_results.name: AX_bipartite_concatenation_psi_symmetry
ai_results.one_line: An explicit family gives ψ(2/7,5/7) ≤ 23/28 < 6/7 = ψ(5/7,2/7).

ai_results.name: AX_direct_product_multipartite_independence_equals_irredundance
ai_results.one_line: A tensor-rank bound retaining the lonely vertices, combined with rank-nonincreasing coordinate compression, proves the conjecture for all complete multipartite factors.

ai_results.name: AX_planar_fvs_face_packing_ratio_2
ai_results.one_line: A 12-vertex planar graph has fvs = 5 and fp = 2; a related family has fvs/fp tending to 3.

ai_results.name: AX_zombie_number_leaf_attachment_invariance
ai_results.one_line: A 59-vertex cactus requires at least three zombies, but adding one leaf produces a graph requiring exactly two.

ai_results.name: AX_list_ramsey_chromatic_family_exact
ai_results.one_line: A greedy assignment of an s-label to every vertex–color pair separates each edge in one of its k listed colors whenever n is at most s^k.

ai_results.name: AX_levine_hat_monotone_success_vanishes
ai_results.one_line: A block-tribes construction gives balanced monotone strategies with success probability arbitrarily close to 1/2 for every number of players, so in fact p_monotone(t)=1/2.

ai_results.name: AX_tournament_clique_number_bounded_witness
ai_results.one_line: For every n at least 3, an explicit circulant tournament on 2n+1 vertices is 3-clique-critical, giving unbounded minimal witnesses already for k=3.

ai_results.name: AX_hypercube_subcube_partitions_dimension_2_asymptotics
ai_results.one_line: A four-layer product construction converts the published lower bound for singleton-and-square partitions of Q_{d-2} into the conjectured number of all-square partitions of Q_d.

ai_results.name: AX_erdos_szekeres_collinear_variant_ell_dependence
ai_results.one_line: An alteration argument gives ES_l(n) <= ceil(l(4 ES_n(n))^((n-1)/(n-2))), so the source bound yields a uniform linear-in-l upper bound matching the lower bound in its l-dependence.

ai_results.name: AX_chromatic_cochromatic_gap_three_small_clique
ai_results.one_line: A 13-vertex circulant-complement seed has (omega,zeta,chi)=(4,4,7), and iterated Mycielski constructions raise zeta and chi together by one while preserving clique number.

ai_results.name: AX_induced_saturated_infinite_tournament_perturbation
ai_results.one_line: The five-vertex tournament C3[TT2,TT2,1] is a counterexample: every countable tournament avoiding it has a distinct locally finite perturbation that still avoids it.

ai_results.name: AX_geometric_graph_plane_path_cover_bound
ai_results.one_line: An odd regular polygon with a central cluster yields point sets requiring at least 3n/4 - O(sqrt(n)) crossing-free paths.

ai_results.name: AX_tournament_color_avoiding_path_non_transitive
ai_results.one_line: Yes: for q=6 and N=9 there is a non-transitive coloring with longest color-avoiding path on 7 vertices, whereas f_{6,5}(9)=8.

ai_results.name: AX_color_balanced_hamilton_cycle_bounds
ai_results.one_line: The requested O(k^2) bound improves to O(k log(k+1)) for Hamilton cycles in both complete and complete bipartite graphs, including for bounded vector labels in an arbitrary norm.

ai_results.name: OPG_orthogonality_graph_circular_chromatic_4
ai_results.one_line: A geometric odd-walk lemma excludes every homomorphism from O to a finite locally bipartite graph, and consequently proves χ_c(O)=4.

ai_results.name: OPG_cycle_powers_equivalence_covering_number_linear
ai_results.one_line: Noncomplete powers of cycles have equivalence covering number Θ(log(k+1)), contradicting the proposed Ω(k) lower bound.

ai_results.name: OPG_3_connected_geodesic_cycles_peripheral_lengths
ai_results.one_line: The eight-vertex graph obtained by inserting a degree-three vertex into every face of a tetrahedron is a counterexample.

ai_results.name: OPG_valency_variety_chromatic_lower_bound
ai_results.one_line: A 37-vertex graph has chromatic number 3 and degree set {0,1,...,29}, making the proposed right-hand side equal to 3; moreover, 37 vertices is minimum.

ill_posed_disclaimer: Attack verdicts are unrefereed model self-reports. An ill-posed label is a diagnostic of the catalog statement supplied to the model, not a literature-review status or a peer-reviewed result.

ill_posed_results.name: AX_ryser_near_extremal_hypergraphs_projective_planes
ill_posed_results.one_line: The catalog item is a research direction rather than a proposition, since “near-extremal,” “large piece,” and “based on a projective plane” have no specified quantitative meanings.
ill_posed_results.caveats: The auxiliary results below require linearity and balanced part sizes and do not settle an additive-stability formulation.

ill_posed_results.name: AX_permutation_property_testing_query_bounds
ill_posed_results.one_line: The catalog item is a research programme rather than a quantified conjecture; moreover, one natural universal Kendall-tau formulation is false in the canonical sampling model.
ill_posed_results.caveats: The negative result below concerns property-independent canonical induced-subpermutation testers, not fixed-property polynomial bounds or adaptive value-query models.

ill_posed_results.name: AX_euclidean_ramsey_l3_vs_lm
ill_posed_results.one_line: As written, the claim is elementary for every m at least 2 with n=1, while including m=1 makes it false.
ill_posed_results.caveats: The catalog statement almost certainly reverses an arrow or misplaces a quantifier.

ill_posed_results.name: AX_avd_edge_coloring_probabilistic_barrier
ill_posed_results.one_line: Without a formal definition of “probabilistic methods” and “on their own,” the stated methodological forecast has no determinate mathematical truth value.
ill_posed_results.caveats: This does not settle the Δ+2 conjecture; only a narrow obstruction to the canonical direct LLL setup is proved below.

ill_posed_results.name: AX_avoidable_non_path_family_existence
ill_posed_results.one_line: As extracted, the question has no determinate truth value because avoidability is defined only for induced path occurrences and no corresponding predicate is specified for non-path graphs.
ill_posed_results.caveats: A finite nonempty two-rooted reformulation could be genuine; below I prove only bounded-family obstructions under one explicit model.

ill_posed_results.name: AX_independent_set_fpt_h_free_candidates
ill_posed_results.one_line: The catalog item is an informal research expectation rather than a proposition, because neither “very few” nor “will end up” specifies a mathematical quantifier or asymptotic notion.
ill_posed_results.caveats: Universal, finite-exception, and density-one reformulations are distinct genuine conjectures and remain unresolved.

ill_posed_results.name: AX_induced_arithmetic_removal_abelian_groups
ill_posed_results.one_line: The quoted conjecture has no determinate truth value, and the most direct uniform finite-group formulation is false.
ill_posed_results.caveats: The counterexamples exploit precisely the unspecified infinite-complexity and torsion/trivial-solution exclusions, so a suitably repaired formulation may remain open.

ill_posed_results.name: AX_surface_excluded_minors_hoppers_exist
ill_posed_results.one_line: The quoted belief has no fixed quantifiers or specified hopper variant, although the natural strong-hopper reading forces a rigid two-unit genus-jump configuration.
ill_posed_results.caveats: The conditional reductions below do not decide existence under the source paper's intended conventions.

ill_posed_results.name: AX_star_contraction_clique_minor_strategy_generality
ill_posed_results.one_line: The quoted sentence is a programmatic methodological suggestion, not a proposition with specified hypotheses, conclusions, or quantifiers.
ill_posed_results.caveats: A particular formalization could become a genuine graph-theoretic problem, but none is specified here.

ill_posed_results.name: AX_outerplanar_strongly_perfect_characterization
ill_posed_results.one_line: The quoted remark does not specify a forbidden family or an if-and-only-if assertion, so it has no determinate truth value as a conjecture.
ill_posed_results.caveats: A precise completeness conjecture may be recoverable from the paper's defined examples, but it is not present in the supplied statement.

ill_posed_results.name: AX_cubic_many_3_edge_colorings_reflexive
ill_posed_results.one_line: The prose claim has no truth value as stated, and its natural absolute-threshold interpretation is false even for connected simple bipartite cubic graphs.
ill_posed_results.caveats: Only absolute or sufficiently low order-dependent counting thresholds are ruled out; no probabilistic, normalized, or high-connectivity meaning of 'tend' was specified.

ill_posed_results.name: AX_twin_width_mis_dominating_approximability
ill_posed_results.one_line: The modal claim has no definite truth value; under the natural fixed-width, supplied-sequence formulation, a constant-factor MIS approximation is equivalent to a PTAS and its existence remains open.
ill_posed_results.caveats: No MIS PTAS or fixed-width hardness is proved; the powering argument assumes a supplied contraction sequence.

ill_posed_results.name: AX_k_colorable_deletion_neighborhood_edge_cover
ill_posed_results.one_line: With the displayed minimum over all n-vertex graphs, m(n,k)=0 identically, while replacing the minimum by a maximum gives a meaningful problem for which only partial results are established below.
ill_posed_results.caveats: This assumes open neighborhoods and induced edges on their union; the catalog may have transcribed max as min.

ill_posed_results.name: AX_k_colorable_deletion_mnk_asymptotics
ill_posed_results.one_line: Under the literal unrestricted definition, m(n,k) has an elementary exact formula, contradicting the quoted n^2/(ek) bound and showing that an H-free hypothesis or some other restriction is missing.
ill_posed_results.caveats: This resolves the formulation supplied here, not the undefined parameter intended in the source paper.

ill_posed_results.name: AX_triangle_removal_vs_dfl_growth
ill_posed_results.one_line: The phrase “similar growth” specifies no asymptotic equivalence, and while the same-parameter Theta interpretation is false, plausible logarithmic or polynomial-equivalence versions remain open.
ill_posed_results.caveats: The argument uses the standard normalization in which N_DFL bounds the number of triangles; edge-count and endpoint conventions only change constants or parameter rescalings.

ill_posed_results.name: AX_ramsey_goodness_books_threshold_not_tight
ill_posed_results.one_line: The phrase "not best possible" has no quantified meaning; the bound is literally improvable for p=2 and k=1, but the intended nondegenerate asymptotic claim is unspecified.
ill_posed_results.caveats: No improvement is obtained for p>=3 and k>=2, and the unverified 2025 article is not used.

ill_posed_results.name: AX_twin_width_matrices_infinite_fields
ill_posed_results.one_line: Without an independent definition of twin-width for rational matrices the claimed equivalence is tautological or undefined; bounded grid rank does satisfy it over every infinite field, while the natural equality-contraction extension is false.
ill_posed_results.caveats: The full source question is truncated, and the grid-rank conclusion uses the precise definition stated below.

ill_posed_results.name: AX_kromatic_claw_free_grassmannian_subvariety
ill_posed_results.one_line: A weak finite-Grassmannian interpretation is trivially true, whereas a faithful stable interpretation requires an unspecified compatible family and already encounters a concrete obstruction for the graph K2.
ill_posed_results.caveats: The sign convention, ambient Grassmannian, stabilization, and meaning of subvariety are unspecified; the likely intended scheme-theoretic stable problem remains open.

ill_posed_results.name: AX_coloring_graph_polynomial_determination
ill_posed_results.one_line: Literally every graph H works by taking H'=H; under the natural requirement H' not isomorphic to H, I prove that every complete graph K_r has the larger witness 2K_r on the class of nonempty graphs.
ill_posed_results.caveats: The intended extra condition on H' is absent; the witness 2K_r is disconnected and fails if the null input graph is allowed.

ill_posed_results.name: AX_domination_packing_ratio_bounded_given_class
ill_posed_results.one_line: With no graph class specified the question has no single answer, and its universal interpretation is false even for the hereditary class of split graphs.
ill_posed_results.caveats: The counterexamples settle only the universal reading; they do not characterize all classes with bounded ratio and may overlap known negative examples.

ill_posed_results.name: AX_largest_clique_minor_opt_approximation
ill_posed_results.one_line: As written, the claim is vacuous via the K_1 solution, and uniform FPT testing in fact yields a polynomial-time approximation with ratio o(OPT) by a timeout construction.
ill_posed_results.caveats: The catalog omits the required restriction on f; no claim is made about a prescribed elementary, power-type, or certifying guarantee.

ill_posed_results.name: AX_small_doubling_sumset_covering_family
ill_posed_results.one_line: As quoted, the conjecture omits essential bounds and quantifiers and hence has no truth value, although natural level-zero and structured special cases admit rigorous coverings.
ill_posed_results.caveats: The exact Conjecture 15 is absent; the conditional results below do not close the global quadratic-in-doubling complexity gap.

ill_posed_results.name: AX_circular_drawing_digraph_forbidden_characterization
ill_posed_results.one_line: The catalog item is a schematic research programme rather than a quantified conjecture, since neither the connectivity class, the containment relation, nor the permitted obstruction type is specified.
ill_posed_results.caveats: Under the standard crossing-free definition, an exact dual criterion and a complete strongly connected 3-connected special case are proved below.
